prompt: Which of the four databases in the lesson does not keep its data in SQLite?

choices.text: Room
choices.why: Room is a layer over the SQLite Android ships.

choices.text: SwiftData
choices.why: SwiftData sits on Core Data, which writes an SQLite file.

choices.text: Realm
choices.why: Right. Realm has an engine and a file format of its own.

choices.text: expo-sqlite
choices.why: It opens the platform's own SQLite.

prompt: A Room query on Android is slow. Where does the lesson say the explanation will be found?

choices.text: In an SQLite query plan
choices.why: Right. Room hands the SQL to SQLite, which decides how to answer it.

choices.text: In Kotlin's coroutine scheduler
choices.why: Coroutines decide which thread waits, not how long the query takes.

choices.text: In the DAO's annotation, which Room rewrites into faster code at compile time
choices.why: Room checks the query at compile time; it does not make it faster.

choices.text: In the Flow the DAO returns
choices.why: The Flow delivers the result; the work is the query's.

prompt: Match each library to what checks its queries, as the lesson's table puts it.

pairs.right: Realm's own engine, when the app runs

right_distractors: the server, before the app is installed

prompt: What did the end of Atlas Device Sync teach, according to the lesson?

choices.text: That SQLite is faster than Realm
choices.why: Speed has nothing to do with what was announced.

choices.text: That object databases cannot work on phones
choices.why: Realm works on phones; the database continues.

choices.text: That a local database should be avoided
choices.why: This whole course argues the opposite.

choices.text: Storage and sync were sold together, and only one stayed
choices.why: Right. An app that relied on the service had to replace its sync, not its storage.

prompt: What does a program need to open an SQLite database on a phone?

choices.text: A database server running on the device, and its port
choices.why: SQLite has no server; it is a library that reads a file.

choices.text: The file
choices.why: Right. The database is one ordinary file in the sandbox.

choices.text: A password the system issues at install time
choices.why: There is no password; the sandbox is the protection.

choices.text: A network connection, to fetch the schema
choices.why: The schema is inside the file.

prompt: A session naming the course `chess`, which does not exist, is inserted through the `sqlite3` shell, and SQLite accepts it. Through `better-sqlite3` it is refused. Why?

choices.text: The shell is an older SQLite that ignores REFERENCES
choices.why: The version is not the reason; the setting is.

choices.text: Foreign-key enforcement is set per connection, on in one and off in the other
choices.why: Right. SQLite leaves them off until PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON.

choices.text: The CHECK constraint
choices.why: CHECK is about minutes, not courses.

choices.text: TypeScript checks the course's id
choices.why: Node removes the types and checks nothing.

prompt: According to week.ts, how many minutes are planned in the week of 2026-10-19?
Why does `s.date < date(?, '+7 days')` find the right sessions when the dates are stored as text?

choices.text: SQLite converts text to dates before it compares them
choices.why: It compares the text; the format is what makes that work.

choices.text: The CHECK constraint guarantees it
choices.why: The CHECK is on minutes.

choices.text: The query reads the dates as numbers of seconds since 1970
choices.why: They are text with no time in them.

choices.text: YYYY-MM-DD sorts as text in the order of the days
choices.why: Right. Year, month, day, each padded, so text order is time order.

prompt: After the index on (course, date), the every-course week query still says `SCAN sessions`. Why?

choices.text: The index is sorted by course first, and the query names none
choices.why: Right. Like a phone book sorted by surname, asked for a first name.

choices.text: SQLite ignores an index until the database is reopened
choices.why: The first query used it straight away.

choices.text: It returns more rows than an index can hold
choices.why: 158 rows is nothing for an index.

choices.text: Dates cannot be indexed
choices.why: The index on date made it a SEARCH.

prompt: In the lesson's run, how many rows did the scan read to return the 8 sessions of one course in one week?

A screen lists one course's sessions in a month. The database has an index on (date, course), and no other. What will EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN most likely show compared with the lesson's (course, date) index?

choices.text: The same SEARCH: column order inside an index does not matter
choices.why: Order is the whole point: the index is sorted by its first column.

choices.text: A SCAN of the table, because the course comes second
choices.why: The date still narrows the rows, so the index helps.

choices.text: A SEARCH on the dates, reading every course's rows in that month
choices.why: Right. It narrows by date, then has to filter the courses out one by one.

choices.text: An error, since the index does not match the query
choices.why: A plan never fails for that; it falls back to what it can use.

prompt: What did the two indexes cost in the lesson's run?

choices.text: A file nearly twice as large
choices.why: Right. Each index repeats columns of every row and is written with it.

choices.text: A slower SEARCH on the course screen
choices.why: The SEARCH is what they bought.

choices.text: Nothing measurable
choices.why: The file grew from 1,015,808 to 1,912,832 bytes.

choices.text: The loss of the primary key
choices.why: The primary key is untouched.

prompt: In batch.ts, session 501 is refused. Without a transaction, what is left in the table?

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: That is the transaction's result.

choices.text: 999 sessions, every one but 501
choices.why: The loop stopped at the error; the rest were never tried.

choices.text: The first 500 sessions
choices.why: Right. Each insert committed on its own, up to the one that failed.

choices.text: 1,000 sessions, with 501 at zero minutes
choices.why: The CHECK refused that row.

prompt: What does putting a download's inserts in one transaction buy? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: a failure leaves the database as it was before
choices.why: Rollback undoes every insert.

choices.text: one wait for the disk instead of one per row
choices.why: One commit, one confirmation.

choices.text: the rows are checked against the server
choices.why: A transaction is local; it knows of no server.

choices.text: the CHECK constraints are skipped for speed
choices.why: They still run; the bad row still fails.

prompt: In WAL mode, while the database is open, two files sit beside planner.db: planner.db-wal and planner.db-___.
An export copies planner.db to the Downloads folder while the app has it open in WAL mode. The person later restores it and the last sessions they added are missing. What happened?

choices.text: The CHECK constraint refused them
choices.why: They were accepted; they were written.

choices.text: They were still in the -wal file, which the copy left out
choices.why: Right. The three files are one database while it is open.

choices.text: SQLite drops the newest rows of a database when its file is copied to another folder
choices.why: SQLite does not know the file was copied.

choices.text: Exports are made in a transaction that was rolled back
choices.why: A file copy is not a transaction.

prompt: Put in order what better-sqlite3 does when `all(batch)` runs and session 501 fails.
items: ROLLBACK, and the error reaches the caller

prompt: A phone's planner downloads 300 sessions from the server and inserts them one statement at a time. The connection drops at row 120 and the app is killed. What does the next launch show, and what is the lesson's fix?

choices.text: A corrupt file; switch WAL on
choices.why: Each insert completed; the file is sound, just half filled.

choices.text: None of them; SQLite waits for the whole download by itself
choices.why: Without a transaction each insert stands alone.

choices.text: 300 sessions, because the network library retries for the app
choices.why: The app was killed; nothing retried.

choices.text: 119 new sessions; insert them in one transaction
choices.why: Right. Half a download is a planner nobody chose; a transaction makes it all or none.
